**The depth:** the longest chain of CRs that wait for one another (each CR's `after`: its `depends.json`, a chain the go approved or the Foreman recorded, the order of a series; a release CR waits for every other CR, one more level).
Say it with the CRs of that chain, in order: "critical path: CR-221 → CR-237 → …".
A parallel batch with no `after` has depth 1.
**The gates:** the CRs still to pass their long gate.
Long gates run one at a time under one lock ([concepts](concepts.md), the long gate), so every CR's gate queues behind the others whatever the slots.
A CR whose project rules exempt it from the long gate (`handback --no-gate`) does not count, nor does a CR covered by a waiver (`order waive`);
under a stack waiver the stack's top counts, once.

Under a rule that asks a local run, every CR of a parallel or series batch that owes the run counts, and the stack's top counts once in a stack, whatever its exemption or waiver (a CR the rules exempt owes none in parallel or series), unless a waiver's words name that gate.
**The two terms, and the floor.** The **lock term** is the gates times the long gate's time.
The **chain term** is the depth times (the long gate's time plus one CI run's time), since a level cannot start before the one under it is handed back ready.
The floor is the larger of the two; the line says which one it is.
**The long gate's time: from the record only.** The latest passed runs of the gate in this project: in the batch's `events.jsonl`, the `gate` events of one `run` share that id;

Read by the Chief of Staff and the Griller at the start of a session, and by the Chief of Staff when it builds the Foreman's prompt (the Foreman's row below).
As soon as the role is set and whenever it changes, the session renames itself by the host's means (its reference); a host that cannot rename: nothing, no workaround.
A title tells first whether the user talks to the session, then the project and the role, with the machine's code in front: a phone shows about 25 characters of a title.
Its parts:
**Machine code:** `[<code>]` first.
The machine's name (the first label of `hostname`) as it is when it has 6 letters or fewer (`Mac`), else its first 6 letters (`Battlestation` gives `Battle`), its first letter uppercase.
A user's word renames the machine for the session only.
In a cloud session (the host's reference says how to tell) the code is `Remote`.
**Icon**, after a space: `💬` for a session the user talks to (the Chief of Staff, a Griller), `⚙️` for one they do not (the Foreman).
**Project**, after a space: the repository's folder name, or, in a surface, the project's folder in it, capitalised (`Chantier`).

**Batch number:** only for a session that steers a batch (the Foreman, the Chief of Staff in direct mode), last, in parentheses after a space as `(Batch <nn>)`, on two digits as in the batch's id (`(Batch 17)`).
**Role:** `CoS` for the Chief of Staff, `Griller`, `Foreman`.
A Griller adds its subject once known, after the role: a few of the user's words, not a slug.
**Separator:** ` · ` (space, U+00B7, space) between the project, the role and a Griller's subject.

| Session | Title | | --- | --- | | Chief of Staff | `[<code>] 💬 Project · CoS` | | Chief of Staff steering a direct batch, from `open --direct`, the hand-over or a switch to direct mode until the batch is closed, then back to the line above | `[<code>] 💬 Project · CoS (Batch <nn>)` | | Griller | `[<code>] 💬 Project · Griller` | | Griller, once its subject is known | `[<code>] 💬 Project · Griller · <subject>` | | Foreman, given in its prompt ([chief-of-staff-batch-start](chief-of-staff-batch-start.md)) | `[<code>] ⚙️ Project · Foreman (Batch <nn>)` |

Examples: `[Battle] 💬 Chantier · CoS`, `[Battle] 💬 Chantier · CoS (Batch 17)`, `[Battle] 💬 Chantier · Griller`, `[Battle] 💬 Chantier · Griller · landing page`, `[Battle] ⚙️ Chantier · Foreman (Batch 17)`, `[Mac] ⚙️ Chantier · Foreman (Batch 06)`, `[Remote] 💬 Chantier · CoS`.
The title given to `seat take --title` is the session's current title; take the seat again (same session, no `--over`) when it changes.
